text: To spot lameness, all pigs/sows in a pen must be made to stand — it can't be assessed while animals are lying down. Lameness matters beyond the leg itself: it stops sows drinking enough (leading to cystitis) and eating enough (leading to constipation and poor performance), and the associated stress weakens immunity. Arthritis: joint inflammation from bacteria, most often Streptococcus in suckling piglets (also Erysipelas) — lameness, swollen joints, visible pain, reluctance to stand; treat promptly with Lincomycin or Amoxicillin to prevent it becoming chronic; prevent in piglets with ½ ml of long-acting Amoxicillin on day 1 of life. Foot rot: infection of the hoof tissue between the claws and at the coronary band, very common on sows kept on poor flooring — painful, swollen claw with a visible coronary-band swelling that can abscess; usually caused by bad cement floors or substandard iron cages (renovating the floor helps if recurrent); treat with Lincomycin/TMP+Sulfa, a 20 cm layer of rice hull to cushion the floor, and OTC spray on the wound. FMD: dramatic, sudden lameness and pain affecting many animals at once, preferring to lie down, screaming/limping badly when forced to move, with blisters at the coronary band and on the snout. CSF: typical laziness and hind-leg weakness — pigs may wander to the feeder but eat little or nothing before lying back down, with a characteristic staggering, 'drunken' walk and tendency to fall into a sitting or lying position. Dog-sitting position (sow sits like a dog, splay-legged, stiff, with sudden acute lameness during or right after lactation): caused by a heavy sow, heavy milk production, low feed intake during lactation, and vitamin D3/calcium shortage; treat with Vitamin D3+Calcium (e.g. Cofacalcium); prevent with 30 g/day of DCP after farrowing. Splay-leg (in piglets, hind legs splayed sideways, unable to stand, easily crushed by the sow, poor viability): treat by taping the hind legs together with 25 mm elastoplast, massaging the muscles, and assisting suckling 2–3 times/day; prevent by injecting the sow with Vitamin E+Selenium weekly for 3 weeks before farrowing.
